Contemporary artificial intelligence (AI) systems predominantly operate under an execution-oriented paradigm in which computational requests are processed as soon as possible after submission. Although immediate computation is essential for latency-sensitive applications, it is not necessarily the most economically efficient strategy for every computational task. Electricity prices fluctuate, GPU rental costs vary, cloud computing resources experience changing supply and demand, and different AI requests exhibit different degrees of tolerance for delayed execution. These conditions suggest that computational efficiency should not be understood exclusively in terms of execution speed. This paper proposes Postponed Computation (PC) as a central temporal computing paradigm in which an AI system deliberately postpones eligible computational operations until a more favorable future execution opportunity becomes available. Unlike conventional post-hoc computation, which analyzes or processes information after an event has occurred, Postponed Computation concerns the intentional scheduling of computation itself for a later time. The paper develops an Economic-Aware Postponed Computation framework for generative AI services, in which the decision to compute is separated from the decision of when to compute. Four principal mechanisms are introduced: User-Adaptive Postponement, Predictive Economic Timing, Deadline-Constrained Postponement, and Cross-Task Aggregation. The framework considers electricity prices, GPU and cloud resource costs, computational availability, waiting costs, service-level commitments, and user-selected execution preferences. A particularly relevant application is an economy-oriented AI service in which eligible user requests, including voluntarily deferred requests from free-tier users, can be retained and executed during periods of lower computational expenditure. The framework further investigates whether compatible requests from multiple users can be aggregated into larger execution batches to improve resource utilization. Existing research has established important foundations in deferred workload scheduling, electricity-aware computing, cloud resource optimization, and inference batching. Accordingly, the contribution of this paper is the formalization and proposed integration of Postponed Computation as a broader temporal decision principle for generative AI services, rather than a claim that workload deferral itself has never been studied. A conceptual architecture, mathematical formulation, operational mechanisms, research hypotheses, and evaluation methodology are presented. No experimental results or empirical performance improvements are claimed.
